neighbours.label: Streams of particles or debris in space and radiation physics (a stream/storm/wave of particles, charged particles, debris), vs everyday 'of' phrases and non-particle physics
fire: The solar wind is a constant stream of charged particles leaving the sun.
A burst of high-energy protons hit the spacecraft during the flare.
Meteors are bits of comet dust burning up in the upper atmosphere.
The beam fires a stream of electrons at the metal target.
A geomagnetic storm of this strength can knock out power grids.
The collision threw clouds of rocky debris into orbit around the planet.
Cosmic rays are showers of particles that rain down from deep space.
Radiation therapy aims charged particles at the tumor.
quiet: The coffee shop has a constant stream of customers in the morning.
A burst of laughter came from the kitchen during dinner.
Meteors are easy to see on a clear night away from city lights.
The teacher fires a list of questions at the class each Monday.
A thunderstorm in the evening cancelled the baseball game.
The movers threw piles of old boxes into the truck.
April showers bring flowers to the garden in May.
Physical therapy aims to strengthen the knee after surgery.
